'''The Slice''' was a wedge-shaped section of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] which began at the edge of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and extended through the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]], the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]], the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], and into the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. The tip of the Slice was known as the [[Arrowhead]], where modern civilization had been founded.<ref name="TEA" /> It was roughly bounded on either side by the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]]. After these two major trade routes were established, the [[Star system/Legends|systems]] of the Slice were rapidly developed as colonists followed the two routes and migrated into the Slice in search of habitable [[Planet/Legends|worlds]].

==Jedi Civil War==
[[File:JediCivilWar.jpg|thumb]]
During the Jedi Civil War which started in 3959 BBY with the surprise attack on Foerost. Revan and Malak launched a massive campaign through the Northern edge of the slice. Assumably to essentially divide the Republic in half and weaken their ability to defend itself.

==Sectors==
*[[Jospro sector/Legends|Jospro sector]]

==Behind the scenes==
Prior to the creation of a full map of the galaxy, the Slice was depicted as being much smaller than currently; sources stated that it contained under a thousand settled planets, and less than 1% of the galaxy. While creating the map, [[Daniel Wallace]] found that those numbers could not be reconciled with his starting info, and he ultimately had to reject them.<ref name="Dan Wallace post">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24648030|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Atlas and Galactic Cartography: Official Discussion|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]]|date=2006-08-11|time=6:05 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801192021/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-atlas-and-galactic-cartography-official-discussion.21938930/page-16}}</ref>
